bandReport.notes: 32 questions, contiguous 89-120, no gaps and no duplicates. p14 opens cleanly at Q89 (printed page 29-A) with its stem and full option block intact, so nothing was left hanging at the end of B3 (which closed at Q88). PAPER ENDS AT Q120 - confirmed four independent ways, and deliberately NOT from P.T.O., which is absent from every page of this band and of B3 and therefore carries no information here. (1) The numbering runs unbroken 89 -> 120 across these four pages and joins B3's unbroken 61 -> 88, so the paper's own count of 120 questions is exactly reached with none left over. (2) Q120 is the last item printed, in the right column of p17, and its (a)-(d) block is complete - the fourth option 'Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat' is fully set, not truncated. (3) An 4x crop of the p17 foot shows the two-column vertical rule STOPPING above the footer, the footer line 'NYRG-B-GNL   ( 35 - A )', and then roughly the bottom eighth of the leaf entirely blank - no continuation, no further question number, no 'P.T.O.'. (4) The page supply is exhausted: the source PDF is 18 pages (indices 0-17) and p17 is the last, so there is nowhere for a Q121 to be. CODE-OPTION ORDERS WERE READ OFF THE PAGE, NOT INFERRED, and this band is the reason that matters - Q91 and Q99 both put the all-three row at (b), NOT at the (d) position where it usually sits: both read (a) 1 only / (b) 1, 2 and 3 / (c) 2 and 3 only / (d) 1 and 2 only, each crop-verified at 7x. That layout also differs from B3's Q75 in the same paper, which runs 1 only / 2 and 3 only / 1 and 3 only / 1, 2 and 3 - so the shape is inconsistent WITHIN this booklet and no option letter may be assumed from another question. Q110's chronology rows were separately crop-verified at 8x as (a) 4-3-2-1 / (b) 2-4-1-3 / (c) 2-1-4-3 / (d) 1-4-3-2. No Match Lists, no figures, graphs, diagrams or circuits anywhere in this band. Devanagari show-through from the Hindi on the reverse of each leaf is present but faint and obscured no English glyph; it was ignored as show-through, not content. Q106's subject term is printed in lower-case italics as 'itat e-dwar' and is transcribed exactly so.
